recognize_zh: 多個紅血球母細胞的細胞核分裂成三到四個小葉，呈苜蓿葉狀（cloverleaf）或核碎裂（karyorrhexis），並有巨母紅血球樣（megaloblastoid）核質發育不同步，這種明顯的紅系發育不良在砷中毒可見。
features: Erythroid precursors with multilobated, cloverleaf-like nuclei and nuclear budding/karyorrhexis
Megaloblastoid erythroblasts with open, finely stippled chromatin and relatively mature polychromatic cytoplasm (nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony)
Binucleate/fragmented nuclear forms in orthochromatic-stage normoblasts
Granulocytic precursors (metamyelocyte/band, myelocytes) with relatively preserved morphology
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows prominent dyserythropoiesis. Numerous erythroid precursors display multilobated, cloverleaf-shaped nuclei, nuclear fragmentation (karyorrhexis) and binucleation, and several larger erythroblasts show megaloblastoid chromatin with nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony. Accompanying granulocytic precursors, including a band form and myelocytes, appear relatively unremarkable. These dyserythropoietic changes are nonspecific but, in the clinical context of arsenic exposure, are consistent with arsenic-induced marrow toxicity mimicking myelodysplasia.

ddx.vs: MDS shows persistent dysplasia often involving multiple lineages with ring sideroblasts or clonal cytogenetic/molecular abnormalities, whereas toxic dyserythropoiesis resolves after exposure removal and lacks clonality.
Megaloblastic anemia also shows nuclear budding and asynchrony but has giant metamyelocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils with low vitamin levels.
CDA presents from childhood with inherited lineage-restricted dyserythropoiesis (e.g., binucleate cells in CDA II, internuclear bridges in CDA I) without toxic exposure.

ddx.dx: Other toxin/drug-induced dysplasia (alcohol, chemotherapy, copper deficiency/zinc excess)
ddx.vs: These produce similar dyserythropoiesis and require history, heavy-metal/copper levels and follow-up marrow to separate.
